input.quote: This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of three (3) years unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0. This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs for a committed three-year initial term (p0104) and Section 5.1 permits termination only "for cause" — uncured material breach, insolvency, acquisition by a competitor, or continuing force majeure (p0107, p0110, p0116). There is no convenience exit for us during the term; the six-month notice in Section 4.0 is only a non-renewal right at term end, and the Purchase Order cancellation right is order-level and subject to cancellation charges. That is walk-away territory under T4C, so we insert a new Section 5.4 giving Customer a 30 days' notice convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and confirming MSL has no convenience right during the initial or any renewal term (preferred position).

ops.text: 5.4 Termination for Convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 30 days' prior written notice to MSL, and MSL shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination. MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a convenience exit for IBM as Customer on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, because Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause during a three-year committed term, and confirmed MSL has no matching convenience right.
proposal.summary: Add Section 5.4 giving Customer (IBM) a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; MSL has no convenience right during a term.

mappings.element: No more than 30 days' written notice.
No Vendor termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
